title: Atropine — Pediatric (bradycardia / RSI premedication)
sources: AHA/AAP 2025 Pediatric Bradycardia With a Pulse Algorithm (atropine 0.02 mg/kg IV/IO, may repeat once; minimum 0.1 mg, maximum single dose 0.5 mg)

changelog.change: Removed the '1 mg (adolescent)' cap: the AHA/AAP 2025 algorithm gives a single 0.5 mg maximum; source made specific.

Content audit Batch 4 housekeeping: category renamed from '...(Adult + Peds)' to '...Pediatric Resuscitation Dosing' — every card in this category was peds-only, the old name was misleading. No dosing content changed.
Added obeseWeightBasis: ideal — hydrophilic resus drug, dose from ideal (age-expected) body weight in an obese child (ERC 2025 / Drug_Dosing_Peds_Weight_Based_Spec).
Initial entry — includes the 0.1 mg minimum-dose floor and revised RSI-premedication indication.

purpose: Symptomatic bradycardia from vagal tone or primary AV block. NOT routine for PEA/asystole. RSI premedication is now narrowly indicated: children < 1 year undergoing direct laryngoscopy, independent of paralytic choice.

doses.indication: Symptomatic bradycardia (vagal / AV block), or RSI premedication in an infant < 1 year for direct laryngoscopy

rule.repeat: May repeat once. Maximum single dose 0.5 mg (AHA/AAP 2025).

doses.notes: Minimum single dose 0.1 mg — smaller doses can cause paradoxical bradycardia. Not indicated for PEA/asystole.

buildNote: Demonstrates minDose flooring. Floor 0.1 mg and cap 0.5 mg per the AHA/AAP 2025 Pediatric Bradycardia With a Pulse algorithm, which gives no separate adolescent cap.
